ESKOM ON A CLIFF FACE

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
LIES AND REVELATIONS, MINISTERS AND BOARDS IMPLICATED AND A UTILITY THAT THREATENS SOUTH AFRICA'S ECONOMY. THIS IS ESKOM NOVEMBER 2017

Unique Selling Point:
CASH STRAPPED
At the beginning of November, the finance minister Malusi Gigaba met with the World bank. Why? Because Eskom is in deep financial trouble and may not be able to pay salaries at the end of January 2018.

Eskom have told South Africa they need R20 billion rand in reserve, but at the end of this month they will only have R1.2 billion. Considering that Eskom burns through R8 billion rand a month its clear the utility is heading over a cliff. But barely 4 months ago when Financial mail flagged exactly this problem, Eskom lied to the South African public and said their finances were stable.


Summary:
Lies, Bribery, insolvency, Ministers implicated and whistleblowers isolated, Eskom's dirty linen is being exposed in Parliament. Meanwhile Eskom has the economy over a barrel. We bring you the latest in this sorry saga





Further information:
FINDING THE MONEY
Municipalities owe Eskom around R11 billion rand, but they can’t pay or won’t pay.

BEGGING AT NERSA
Now Eskom are bleating at NERSA and want an above average inflation increase of 19.9 % a decision says the manufacturing circle that could lead to massive job losses and company shut downs. On December 7th NERSA will announce the increases. The problem for consumers is that we are damned if we do, and damned if we don’t. If Eskom gets its way, the economy is likely to contract further. If not they will need a bail out. In fact, they may need a bail out anyway as Finance Minister Malusi Gigaba has stated in his medium- term budget policy statement that Eskom is the single biggest risk to the economy.

BIG NUMBERS
Eskom’s debt has ballooned and despite still having the backing of government guarantees to the tune of R350bn, sources for funding are becoming more difficult to find. Government guarantees imply that Eskom can secure lenders, because the government will bail them out, but lenders don’t want to lend Eskom any more money as they watch in horror at the complete absence of corporate governance at the utility.
South Africa has R477.7bn of guarantees available for public institutions. Of that, R308.3bn has been used. Information from Treasury indicates that Eskom is the biggest recipient, having used R218.2bn of the R350bn available to it by the end of the last financial year.
Chief financial officer Anoj Singh said that Eskom’s debt is expected to peak at R500bn.
A STRANGE ECONOMIC MODEL
Eskom now has too much electricity as prices rise and the economy contracts. But instead of lowering the tariff – Eskom are doing the opposite and want to increase the tariff – going against fundamental market principals.

THE SNAKES SLITHERING OUT OF PANDORA’S BOX
Each week the Eskom Inquiry in Parliament quietly gets on with its work. Coming out of this enquiry are astonishing revelation that link ministers and deputy ministers to the Gupta family. Whistleblowers have accused Minister Brown of lying, obfuscating and feigning ignorance. Former CEO’s have hammered the board. Board members have implicated two of the former chair persons in wrong doing. Those revealing the truth like head of Legal at Eskom, Suzanne Daniels and former board spokesman Khulani Quoma have been villiefied by Eskom and isolated. But clearly the inquiry is hitting a nerve.

A BRIBE BY A MINISTER?
On Sunday 19th November 2017, the Sunday Times revealed that Minister of State Security Bongani Bongo tried to bribe the chair of the committee Advocate Vanarra. He has signed an affidavit and given it to the speaker. The MP’s have asked for this matter to be urgently investigated

THE CASE AGAINST MR KOKO
Meanwhile Mr Koko’s sham disciplinary is about to get underway. He wants his job back and those that have watched the disciplinary unfold believe Mr. Koko has every chance of getting his job back

MEANWHILE THE CLOCK TICKS AND ESKOM AND THE MINISTER HAVE DONE NOTHING.

Press Release:


Eskom on Edge
As Eskom teeters on the edge of bankruptcy, what are the executives at Megawatt Park doing? So far
there have been some explosive allegations at the Parliamentary inquiry on state-owned enterprises and
last week President Zuma was implicated by a former chairperson of the board. But despite reports of
attempted bribery to collapse the inquiry, Advocate Vanara pressed on, leading MPs through the mists of
Eskom scandals. This week former CEO Brian Molefe was in court defending his R30 million payout and
Matshela Koko’s disciplinary draws to a close in the wake of ratings agencies downgrading Eskom.

Script:


CHRONICLES OF ESKOM FINAL SCRIPT 14.12


TITLE: CASH CRUNCH

Commentary One
Eskom is in deep financial trouble. This week it was downgraded by two ratings agencies

Sikonathi Mantshantsha
Eskom is the single biggest risk to the country, if you have Lynne Brown there
you are sinking South Africa

Commentary two
Deputy Editor of the financial Mail, Sikonathi Mantshantsha has been at the forefront of exposing Eskom malfeasance. He warned back inJuly that Eskom would run out of money, round about now. Not so, said acting CEO Johnny Dladla and Eskom interim chairman Zethembe Khoza when the Mail and Guardian asked for clarity

Up Sound Phillip De wet
Gentleman can you give us a clear and unambiguous answer: is Eskom in financial distress?
Johnny Dladla
The answer is an emphatic no
Zithemba Khoza
We are financially sound and stable

Commentary Three
But nothing could be further from the truth. Burdened by a debt book of R471 billion, the real picture of Eskom’s finances has been presented in a quarterly report to minister Lynne Brown, and seen by Energy analyst Chris Yelland

Chris Yelland
It’s quite alarming! By the end of November, Eskom are likely to have about R1.2 billion. By the end of January next year, their forecast is to have minus five billion rand

Commentary Four
Right now, they are down to their last R1.2 billion rand.

Sikonathi
Eskom is bankrupt. R1.2 billion rand will only pay the drivers of the coal, not the companies that dig it out

EXECUTIVES OF THE SAXONWOLD SHEBEEN

Former CEO Brian Molefe, former CFO Anoj Singh, former chairman of the board Dr Ben Ngubane and Matshela Koko, have presided over Eskom’s downward spiral. They have been exposed by journalists, reports and whistleblowers. Never mind Eskom, they are fighting to save their own skins.

Devi
So did you prepay
Koko
I suspect that’s the case
Devi
But Mr Koko you said no
Koko
I suspect that is the case

Commentary five
Matshela Koko was caught lying on Carte Blanche, then he was exposed by the Sunday times for a multimillion rand tender given to his step daughter. He told a disciplinary committee this week it was a smear campaign because he was cleaning up corruption.

On Wednesday, Brian Molefe was in court – hoping to keep his R30 million pension payout and get his job as the head of Eskom back, and November also saw Dr Ben Ngubane facing down charges of forging share certificates

Anoj Singh
I can go on record saying I have not received a bribe from anybody

Commentary Six
Anoj Singh controlled Eskom’s finances. Gupta leaks exposed Singh enjoying ten thousand rand’s worth of massages in Dubai, paid for by the Gupta’s. He was only suspended when the Development bank threatened to call in its loan if action wasn’t taken against him.

Anoj Singh
As I said to you before I will be submitting a tell all document so lets just wait for that

Commentary Seven
Four months later we wait. But the real tell all, has been happening here in Parliament, at the inquiry into state capture of state owned enterprises.

LINK
It seems the Eskom inquiry is touching a nerve. Minister Lynne Brown called it a Kangaroo court and now we hear allegations that the State Security minister tried to bribe its evidence leader Advocate Vanara

Commentary eight
But advocate Vanara reportedly made a sworn affidavit, gave it to the speaker and pressed on, leading his committee of MP’s through the mists of countless Eskom scandals.

A BRAVE WHISTLEBLOWER

Commentary nine
Former board spokesman Khulani Qoma was hired to restore Eskom’ reputation,
He wrote a letter to the board recommending the removal of Koko and Singh, which almost got him fired. He has been isolated at Eskom. They have distanced themselves from his comments at the inquiry

Khulani Qoma former board spokesman
So the problem here is the minister. She will either say I have been lied to or I don’t know or something to that effect /this minister needs to sit and account. This mess would not have been possible if she was a capable minister. She is totally incapable

Commentary ten
How was it possible he asked, that Anoj Singh could be suspended, but chairman of the board Zethembe Khoza could ask the minister in this letter for permission for Singh to get the minutes and attend board meetings

Khulani
It would puzzle anyone who knows anything about governance – that when you are suspended you don’t have access to these things and the minister didn’t see anything wrong with this because she still kept this board

THE BUCK STOPS NOWHERE

Commentary eleven
Lynne Brown was a reluctant witness before the committee. She complained of untested allegations and said the media and opposition parties have chosen Eskom as their battleground ahead of the elective conference.

Lynne Brown
It presently feels as if Eskom has been beaten to the ground and is being pinned down by the weight of untested allegations while being kicked to death

Commentary twelve
The minister said that the best thing for the country, the economy, Eskom and her personally, is a comprehensive investigation. But MP Pravin Gordhan was scathing.

Pravin
So on the one side of the scale we have all the coal purchase controversies, the IT system controversies, the boards that are dominated by Gupta linked people, suspensions of people that are actually innocent…..

Commentary thirteen
For over two minutes, Gordhan listed the many shocking transgressions under Minister Brown’s watch

Pravin
You have the prepayment that Mr. Singh agreed to, which eventually was used …
All So on the one side we have all of …..and on the other side, as far as the public is concerned all we have is denials, I end my case. Thank you




OTHER PEOPLES MONEY – OURS

Commentary fourteen
Suzanne Daniels was company secretary and later head of legal. She worked closely with the CFO Anoj Singh and Matshela Koko, and has meticulous records of the deals that went down. One of those is how Eskom helped the Gupta’s buy Optimum mine, an arrangement that Advocate Vanara and the MPS are interested in

Advocate Vanara
If the R1.6 billion was facilitated by Eskom, the R600 million came from Eskom and a portion of the purchase price came from Trillian who happened to be paid by Eskom under very dubious circumstances, do we see this OPM concept at play here?
Suzanne Daniels
From all the evidence and what I know now, this is definitely a case of OPM

TAKE ME TO YOUR GUPTA

Commentary fifteen
Brian Dames was the Chief executive of Eskom from 2010 to 2014 and it was under his watch the Gupta’s made their first brazen overtures. Finally he revealed the truth.

Brian Dames
It went like this: It was decided we can work with you, I don’t know who we was, it was strange …..it needed no additional coal

Clair
Brian Dames said that he was also taken to meet the Gupta’s?
Sikonathi
By the advisor to Malusi Gigaba.

Up sound Brian Dames
I was quite angry, I was very angry told them never to bring those people to me again

Commentary sixteen
When Mantshantsha had pressed Dames on why he left Eskom he told him the story on condition it was kept confidential

Sikonathi
he told me about death threats and helicopter accidents and he told me exactly what he repeated that day in parliament

Brian Dames
I was quite angry. I was very angry I actually called Mr Mahlangu and said you will not bring these people to me again




Commentary seventeen
Fast forward to 2017 when Daniels swears under oath that she too was taken to meet with Ajay Gupta, Duduzane Zuma and to her surprise Deputy minister Ben Martins at a flat in Melrose Arch

Suzanne
Mr. Gupta was in a grey tracksuit pants no shoes and a t-shirt/ I felt like I was in a movie because here was this man, there was Duduzane and there was Ben Martins. Ben Martins was the deputy minister of Public enterprises

Commentary eighteen
She alleged they seemed to be trying to manipulate Brian Molefe’s court dates till after this December. Ben Martins has denied her allegations and called her a liar and a clueless ignoramus.

Suzanne Daniels
I couldn’t believe where I was and what I was hearing /I left, went home, poured myself a stiff shot of whisky and went to sleep.

MARCH OF THE CEO’S

Commentary nineteen
After Dames, Tshedisa Matona came in as the next permanent CEO. But Matona would last only seven months before he was suspended and forced out, even though he was innocent of any wrong doing.

Then last week a bombshell, as former Board chair Zola Tsotsi implicated President Zuma and SAA board chair Dudu Myeni as the real decision makers to remove Matona.

Zola Tsotsi
What Myeni said to me is that I should please come to the residence for an audience with the president

Commentary twenty
Tsotsi said he was shocked when instructed by Dudu Myeni to remove Matona in the presidents presence. Then came the calls from the international financiers

Zola Tsotsi
I was to have the most unpleasant and humiliating experience of my career at Eskom. The head of our investors from across the world would be asking for an explanation trying to defend what was an indefensible position

Commentary twenty-one
The removal of Matona and three other executives led S and P to downgrade Eskom to junk. In the shadows -the Gupta’s who Tsotsi alleges he met them at Minister Browns home- a charge she has vigorously denied



Lynne Brown
I have never consulted with anyone on my executive functions, not Tony Gupta or Salim Essa or anyone else

Commentary twenty- two
Soon, the new board turned on Tsotsi

Zola Tsotsi
I was approached by Tony Gupta who requested we meet. At the meeting Tony told me, and I quote he said: Chairman you are not helping us with anything. We are the ones who put you into this position. We are the ones who can take you out

Commentary Twenty- three
he resigned under duress


BONANZA TIME

Commentary twenty four
In came Brian Molefe and board chair Dr Ben Ngubane and the stage was set.
Gupta coal contracts ballooned to at least R14 billion. By 2016, Tegeta was supplying Arnot, Hendrina, Komati and Majuba power stations. Their Brakfontein mine supplied Majuba with the most expensive but worst quality coal, compared to other Majuba suppliers at the time. But still the Gupta’s wanted more, and their associated company, Trillian billed Eskom R564 million rand for consultancy work without a contract

Suzanne Daniels
In my view, based on what I know now, there is only one way to describe this. This is brazen theft

MEDUPI AND KUSILE BLEED

Commentary twenty five
Kusile alone has cost Eskom R160 billion rand and it needs another R40 billion to complete. Eskom are hoping for a 20% tariff increase to plug the gap. But that won’t be enough says Dr Grove Steyn, whose company Meridian has done a study that could save Eskom R17 billion rand

Grove
We estimated that if Eskom decommission Hendrina Komati and Grootvlei earlier they could save roughly R12.5 billion and then we think its plausible if Kusile units 5 and 6 are not completed that saving could increase to R17 billion.

Commentary twenty- six
But is anyone listening?






HELD TO RANSOM

Commentary Twenty-seven
And just when you thought the Gupta’s grip over Eskom may have loosened, Amabhungane broke the news this week that the Gupta owned Optimum mine threatened to stop the conveyer belts delivering coal to Hendrina Power station.

They want more money for their coal.

This week Eskom were scrambling around to ensure Hendrina doesn’t shut down. If things don’t change, January 2018 could begin like January 2008, in the dark.

THE END



PROMO ONE 15 seconds

Commentary
As 2017 comes to an end, Eskom is in deep financial trouble.

Sikonathi
Eskom is bankrupt. R1.2 billion rand will only pay the drivers of the coal, not the companies that dig it out

PROMO TWO 15 seconds

Commentary
Startling revelations, lies, threats of intimidation, allegations of bribery and a president implicated. It’s all happening at the Parliamentary Inquiry into state capture as Eskom’s dirty secrets are revealed.


PROMO THREE 10 seconds

Suzanne
Mr. Gupta was in a grey tracksuit pants no shoes and a t-shirt.
Commentary
Next week the parliamentary inquiry into State- owned enterprises continues

He was only suspended when the Development bank threatened to call in its loan if action wasn’t taken against him. Anoj Singh As I said to you before I will be submitting a tell all document so lets just wait for that Commentary Seven Four months later we wait. But the real tell all, has been happening here in Parliament, at the inquiry into state capture of state owned enterprises. LINK It seems the Eskom inquiry is touching a nerve. Minister Lynne Brown called it a Kangaroo court and now we hear allegations that the State Security minister tried to bribe its evidence leader Advocate Vanara Commentary eight But advocate Vanara reportedly made a sworn affidavit, gave it to the speaker and pressed on, leading his committee of MP’s through the mists of countless Eskom scandals. A BRAVE WHISTLEBLOWER Commentary nine Former board spokesman Khulani Qoma was hired to restore Eskom’ reputation, He wrote a letter to the board recommending the removal of Koko and Singh, which almost got him fired. He has been isolated at Eskom. They have distanced themselves from his comments at the inquiry Khulani Qoma former board spokesman So the problem here is the minister. She will either say I have been lied to or I don’t know or something to that effect /this minister needs to sit and account. This mess would not have been possible if she was a capable minister. She is totally incapable Commentary ten How was it possible he asked, that Anoj Singh could be suspended, but chairman of the board Zethembe Khoza could ask the minister in this letter for permission for Singh to get the minutes and attend board meetings Khulani It would puzzle anyone who knows anything about governance – that when you are suspended you don’t have access to these things and the minister didn’t see anything wrong with this because she still kept this board THE BUCK STOPS NOWHERE Commentary eleven Lynne Brown was a reluctant witness before the committee. She complained of untested allegations and said the media and opposition parties have chosen Eskom as their battleground ahead of the elective conference. Lynne Brown It presently feels as if Eskom has been beaten to the ground and is being pinned down by the weight of untested allegations while being kicked to death Commentary twelve The minister said that the best thing for the country, the economy, Eskom and her personally, is a comprehensive investigation. But MP Pravin Gordhan was scathing. Pravin So on the one side of the scale we have all the coal purchase controversies, the IT system controversies, the boards that are dominated by Gupta linked people, suspensions of people that are actually innocent….. Commentary thirteen For over two minutes, Gordhan listed the many shocking transgressions under Minister Brown’s watch Pravin You have the prepayment that Mr. Singh agreed to, which eventually was used … All So on the one side we have all of …..and on the other side, as far as the public is concerned all we have is denials, I end my case. Thank you OTHER PEOPLES MONEY – OURS Commentary fourteen Suzanne Daniels was company secretary and later head of legal. She worked closely with the CFO Anoj Singh and Matshela Koko, and has meticulous records of the deals that went down. One of those is how Eskom helped the Gupta’s buy Optimum mine, an arrangement that Advocate Vanara and the MPS are interested in Advocate Vanara If the R1.6 billion was facilitated by Eskom, the R600 million came from Eskom and a portion of the purchase price came from Trillian who happened to be paid by Eskom under very dubious circumstances, do we see this OPM concept at play here? Suzanne Daniels From all the evidence and what I know now, this is definitely a case of OPM TAKE ME TO YOUR GUPTA Commentary fifteen Brian Dames was the Chief executive of Eskom from 2010 to 2014 and it was under his watch the Gupta’s made their first brazen overtures. Finally he revealed the truth. Brian Dames It went like this: It was decided we can work with you, I don’t know who we was, it was strange …..it needed no additional coal Clair Brian Dames said that he was also taken to meet the Gupta’s? Sikonathi By the advisor to Malusi Gigaba. Up sound Brian Dames I was quite angry, I was very angry told them never to bring those people to me again Commentary sixteen When Mantshantsha had pressed Dames on why he left Eskom he told him the story on condition it was kept confidential Sikonathi he told me about death threats and helicopter accidents and he told me exactly what he repeated that day in parliament Brian Dames I was quite angry. I was very angry I actually called Mr Mahlangu and said you will not bring these people to me again Commentary seventeen Fast forward to 2017 when Daniels swears under oath that she too was taken to meet with Ajay Gupta, Duduzane Zuma and to her surprise Deputy minister Ben Martins at a flat in Melrose Arch Suzanne Mr. Gupta was in a grey tracksuit pants no shoes and a t-shirt/ I felt like I was in a movie because here was this man, there was Duduzane and there was Ben Martins. Ben Martins was the deputy minister of Public enterprises Commentary eighteen She alleged they seemed to be trying to manipulate Brian Molefe’s court dates till after this December. Ben Martins has denied her allegations and called her a liar and a clueless ignoramus. Suzanne Daniels I couldn’t believe where I was and what I was hearing /I left, went home, poured myself a stiff shot of whisky and went to sleep. MARCH OF THE CEO’S Commentary nineteen After Dames, Tshedisa Matona came in as the next permanent CEO. But Matona would last only seven months before he was suspended and forced out, even though he was innocent of any wrong doing. Then last week a bombshell, as former Board chair Zola Tsotsi implicated President Zuma and SAA board chair Dudu Myeni as the real decision makers to remove Matona. Zola Tsotsi What Myeni said to me is that I should please come to the residence for an audience with the president Commentary twenty Tsotsi said he was shocked when instructed by Dudu Myeni to remove Matona in the presidents presence. Then came the calls from the international financiers Zola Tsotsi I was to have the most unpleasant and humiliating experience of my career at Eskom. The head of our investors from across the world would be asking for an explanation trying to defend what was an indefensible position Commentary twenty-one The removal of Matona and three other executives led S and P to downgrade Eskom to junk. In the shadows -the Gupta’s who Tsotsi alleges he met them at Minister Browns home- a charge she has vigorously denied Lynne Brown I have never consulted with anyone on my executive functions, not Tony Gupta or Salim Essa or anyone else Commentary twenty- two Soon, the new board turned on Tsotsi Zola Tsotsi I was approached by Tony Gupta who requested we meet. At the meeting Tony told me, and I quote he said: Chairman you are not helping us with anything. We are the ones who put you into this position. We are the ones who can take you out Commentary Twenty- three he resigned under duress BONANZA TIME Commentary twenty four In came Brian Molefe and board chair Dr Ben Ngubane and the stage was set. Gupta coal contracts ballooned to at least R14 billion. By 2016, Tegeta was supplying Arnot, Hendrina, Komati and Majuba power stations. Their Brakfontein mine supplied Majuba with the most expensive but worst quality coal, compared to other Majuba suppliers at the time. But still the Gupta’s wanted more, and their associated company, Trillian billed Eskom R564 million rand for consultancy work without a contract Suzanne Daniels In my view, based on what I know now, there is only one way to describe this. This is brazen theft MEDUPI AND KUSILE BLEED Commentary twenty five Kusile alone has cost Eskom R160 billion rand and it needs another R40 billion to complete. Eskom are hoping for a 20% tariff increase to plug the gap. But that won’t be enough says Dr Grove Steyn, whose company Meridian has done a study that could save Eskom R17 billion rand Grove We estimated that if Eskom decommission Hendrina Komati and Grootvlei earlier they could save roughly R12.5 billion and then we think its plausible if Kusile units 5 and 6 are not completed that saving could increase to R17 billion. Commentary twenty- six But is anyone listening? HELD TO RANSOM Commentary Twenty-seven And just when you thought the Gupta’s grip over Eskom may have loosened, Amabhungane broke the news this week that the Gupta owned Optimum mine threatened to stop the conveyer belts delivering coal to Hendrina Power station. They want more money for their coal. This week Eskom were scrambling around to ensure Hendrina doesn’t shut down. If things don’t change, January 2018 could begin like January 2008, in the dark. THE END PROMO ONE 15 seconds Commentary As 2017 comes to an end, Eskom is in deep financial trouble. Sikonathi Eskom is bankrupt. R1.2 billion rand will only pay the drivers of the coal, not the companies that dig it out PROMO TWO 15 seconds Commentary Startling revelations, lies, threats of intimidation, allegations of bribery and a president implicated. It’s all happening at the Parliamentary Inquiry into state capture as Eskom’s dirty secrets are revealed. PROMO THREE 10 seconds Suzanne Mr. Gupta was in a grey tracksuit pants no shoes and a t-shirt. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): LIES AND REVELATIONS, MINISTERS AND BOARDS IMPLICATED AND A UTILITY THAT THREATENS SOUTH AFRICA'S ECONOMY. THIS IS ESKOM NOVEMBER 2017
metadata.Unique Selling Point: CASH STRAPPED At the beginning of November, the finance minister Malusi Gigaba met with the World bank. Why? Because Eskom is in deep financial trouble and may not be able to pay salaries at the end of January 2018. Eskom have told South Africa they need R20 billion rand in reserve, but at the end of this month they will only have R1.2 billion. Considering that Eskom burns through R8 billion rand a month its clear the utility is heading over a cliff. But barely 4 months ago when Financial mail flagged exactly this problem, Eskom lied to the South African public and said their finances were stable.
metadata.Summary: Lies, Bribery, insolvency, Ministers implicated and whistleblowers isolated, Eskom's dirty linen is being exposed in Parliament. Meanwhile Eskom has the economy over a barrel. We bring you the latest in this sorry saga
metadata.Further information: FINDING THE MONEY Municipalities owe Eskom around R11 billion rand, but they can’t pay or won’t pay. BEGGING AT NERSA Now Eskom are bleating at NERSA and want an above average inflation increase of 19.9 % a decision says the manufacturing circle that could lead to massive job losses and company shut downs. On December 7th NERSA will announce the increases. The problem for consumers is that we are damned if we do, and damned if we don’t. If Eskom gets its way, the economy is likely to contract further. If not they will need a bail out. In fact, they may need a bail out anyway as Finance Minister Malusi Gigaba has stated in his medium- term budget policy statement that Eskom is the single biggest risk to the economy. BIG NUMBERS Eskom’s debt has ballooned and despite still having the backing of government guarantees to the tune of R350bn, sources for funding are becoming more difficult to find. Government guarantees imply that Eskom can secure lenders, because the government will bail them out, but lenders don’t want to lend Eskom any more money as they watch in horror at the complete absence of corporate governance at the utility. South Africa has R477.7bn of guarantees available for public institutions. Of that, R308.3bn has been used. Information from Treasury indicates that Eskom is the biggest recipient, having used R218.2bn of the R350bn available to it by the end of the last financial year. Chief financial officer Anoj Singh said that Eskom’s debt is expected to peak at R500bn. A STRANGE ECONOMIC MODEL Eskom now has too much electricity as prices rise and the economy contracts. But instead of lowering the tariff – Eskom are doing the opposite and want to increase the tariff – going against fundamental market principals. THE SNAKES SLITHERING OUT OF PANDORA’S BOX Each week the Eskom Inquiry in Parliament quietly gets on with its work. Coming out of this enquiry are astonishing revelation that link ministers and deputy ministers to the Gupta family. Whistleblowers have accused Minister Brown of lying, obfuscating and feigning ignorance. Former CEO’s have hammered the board. Board members have implicated two of the former chair persons in wrong doing. Those revealing the truth like head of Legal at Eskom, Suzanne Daniels and former board spokesman Khulani Quoma have been villiefied by Eskom and isolated. But clearly the inquiry is hitting a nerve. A BRIBE BY A MINISTER? On Sunday 19th November 2017, the Sunday Times revealed that Minister of State Security Bongani Bongo tried to bribe the chair of the committee Advocate Vanarra. He has signed an affidavit and given it to the speaker. The MP’s have asked for this matter to be urgently investigated THE CASE AGAINST MR KOKO Meanwhile Mr Koko’s sham disciplinary is about to get underway. He wants his job back and those that have watched the disciplinary unfold believe Mr. Koko has every chance of getting his job back MEANWHILE THE CLOCK TICKS AND ESKOM AND THE MINISTER HAVE DONE NOTHING.
